title: Ransomware encrypting a file server
description: Mass file renames to .locked, ransom note README_RESTORE.txt in every share, volume shadow copies deleted via vssadmin.
steps: Disconnect the server from the network immediately
Identify patient zero from SMB write logs
Check backups are intact and offline
Collect the ransomware binary for analysis
root_cause: Compromised VPN account without MFA used to reach the file server
remediation: Isolated server, restored from offline backup, reset all VPN credentials, enforced MFA
outcome: Confirmed malicious, data restored from backup
feedback: Helpful: isolation first was the right call
lessons: Shadow copy deletion plus mass renames means contain first and investigate second. Verify backups before anything else

title: Local admin added by a standard user
description: A standard user account was added to the local Administrators group minutes after an unsigned installer ran.
steps: Identify who made the change from the security event log
Hash and submit the installer
Review the user's recent downloads
Remove the account from the group
root_cause: Exploit of an unpatched local privilege escalation flaw by a trojanized installer
remediation: Removed admin rights, reimaged host, patched the vulnerable component
lessons: Group membership changes right after an unsigned binary runs are a strong escalation signal

title: Impossible travel sign-in for finance user
description: Successful sign-ins from Mumbai and then Lagos 20 minutes apart, followed by a new mailbox forwarding rule.
steps: Review sign-in logs and device IDs
Check mailbox rules and OAuth app consents
Revoke sessions and reset password
Check whether MFA was bypassed
remediation: Revoked sessions, reset password, removed the forwarding rule, re-registered MFA
outcome: Confirmed malicious, no data confirmed lost
feedback: Partially helpful: should have checked for the forwarding rule earlier
lessons: Impossible travel plus a new mailbox rule means account takeover. Check rules and consented apps

title: Large archive upload to cloud storage at night
description: 4 GB zip uploaded to an unsanctioned file-sharing site at 02:10, preceded by bulk reads of the engineering share.
steps: Confirm upload size and destination in proxy logs
Review file access logs on the source share
Interview the user's manager
Preserve the host image
remediation: Disabled account, blocked the site, legal and HR notified
lessons: Off-hours bulk reads followed by a large upload to a personal file-sharing site point to insider exfiltration

title: Web shell on public web server
description: New file uploads/img/logo.php executing system commands. Access log shows POST requests from one IP.
steps: Preserve the web root and logs
Find the initial upload request
Check for other new PHP files
Isolate the server
root_cause: Unrestricted file upload flaw in the CMS plugin
remediation: Removed the shell, patched the plugin, rebuilt the server, rotated database credentials
lessons: A PHP file in an uploads directory is almost always malicious. Find the upload request, then assume credential theft

title: Regular beaconing to a rare domain
description: Connections every 60 seconds with tiny payloads from WS-014 to a domain first seen 2 days ago.
steps: Check domain age and reputation
Identify the originating process
Search for the same domain across all hosts
Isolate the host
root_cause: Command-and-control beaconing from malware left by a phishing macro
remediation: Isolated host, blocked domain and IP, reimaged host
feedback: Helpful: matched the C2 domain from an earlier incident
lessons: Fixed-interval small connections to a newly registered domain are beaconing. Search the domain across all hosts

title: Phishing email with ISO attachment
description: User opened an ISO from a purchase-order email that mounted and launched a shortcut file running PowerShell.
steps: Find the email and all recipients
Pull the ISO and LNK for analysis
Check for PowerShell launched by explorer.exe
Isolate the host
root_cause: Malicious ISO used to bypass mark-of-the-web controls
remediation: Isolated host, purged email org-wide, blocked ISO attachments at the gateway
lessons: ISO or LNK attachments leading to PowerShell are phishing delivery. Purge from all mailboxes quickly

title: Encoded PowerShell from IT inventory script
description: Alert on powershell.exe -enc launched by the IT management agent on a schedule every Monday at 06:00.
steps: Check the parent process and signature
Decode the command and compare with the known inventory script
Confirm the schedule with the IT team
remediation: Added a documented exception for the signed agent on SRV-MGMT-01 only
feedback: Helpful: would have been quick if the parent process was checked first
lessons: Encoded PowerShell is not always malicious. Verify the parent process, signature and schedule before escalating
